title: 3-Read Friday #28: Improving Teaching, Student Absence, and Targeting Indicators
author: Craig Barton
summary: Issue 28 leads with an anonymous headteacher's ten best bets for improving teaching, which Barton frames through his own school-visit consultancy practice, where headteacher conversations about teaching and learning priorities are a recurring feature of his work - he calls the post gold for anyone with leadership responsibilities. His second pick, Mrs Cox's piece on managing intermittent student absence in RE, is introduced with unusual editorial modesty, Barton stating plainly that there's no simple fix before crediting her with three specific, subject-tested strategies. His third selection, Adam Boxer's "Targeting indicators," gets traced back to a specific influence in Barton's own network: Sammy Kempner, a guest on his Tips for Teachers podcast, whom Barton credits with first making the underlying principle - ask the students least likely to know an answer for a reliable understanding check - click for him. The issue illustrates how Barton's curation draws connective tissue between outside bloggers and his own professional ecosystem rather than presenting picks as free-floating recommendations.
points: Barton frames South Glous Head's piece through his own consultancy work, noting he regularly sits down with headteachers to discuss teaching and learning priorities, positioning the anonymous head's ten best bets as directly useful to that recurring conversation.

His summary of Mrs Cox's absence piece is deliberately modest, stating upfront there are no simple solutions before crediting her with three practical, subject-specific strategies rather than a general theory.

Barton traces the intellectual lineage of Adam Boxer's targeting-indicators concept to a specific guest, Sammy Kempner, on his own Tips for Teachers podcast, crediting Kempner with first making the underlying principle click for him.

The issue connects two Barton-adjacent sources (his own podcast guest, his own school-visit conversations) to external bloggers, showing how his curation draws on and reinforces his own professional network and back-catalogue.
quotes: During most of my school visits, I have an opportunity to sit down with the headteacher to discuss their teaching and learning priorities and the challenges they are facing.

This wonderful post shares the 10 best bets from an experienced headteacher on how they try to improve teaching and learning in their school. This is gold for any headteacher, but also anyone with leadership responsibilities.
There are no simple solutions to the problem of student absences, but in this thoughtful blog, Mrs Cox shares three practical strategies that she uses successfully in her subject, RE.

It was Sammy Kempner, on my Tips for Teachers podcast, who first hammered home to me the importance of asking the students least likely to know the correct answer if you want a reliable check for understanding.
Adam shares some practical ways we can do this in the latest instalment of his excellent Most Common Actions series.
